confirmed_material_findings.title: Represent lawful unresolved absolute world time without requiring a numeric interval or repair

locations.role: closed time slot and interval/repair requirement
T192/T195 preserve ordinary time semantics but omit a specific accepted unresolved-time branch

confirmed_material_findings.scenario: After declining, a genuine ordinary result resolves a plot-driven time skip with a complete calendar-only setWorldTime (year, monthName, dayOfMonth, timeOfDay), with no currentTimeInMinutes. This is a currently lawful ordinary command, including when the client cannot convert that calendar to numeric minutes.
confirmed_material_findings.requirement: Every currently lawful ordinary outcome must resolve through its actual owners; decline must preserve their existing time behavior without unsupported refusal, invented elapsed time, or new validation requirements.
evidence: ValidationService.QuestsRivalsFactionsAndWorld.cs:1831-1875 validates the complete calendar command and explicitly states at 1870 that currentTimeInMinutes is optional and the scheduler must fail open when it is absent.

ProgressionScheduleService.MortalJointInputs.cs:84-91 skips ValidateMortalOutcome for HasUnresolvedAbsoluteOverride; ApplyMortalOutcomeFromInputs at 125-142 takes the maximum of existing fallback/report/control values instead of requiring repair.
ProgressionScheduleService.MortalJointBasis.cs:167-186 preserves the unresolved flag when a complete absolute date has no numeric minutes.
EffectAcceptedTurnInputComposer.cs:707-737 yields null numeric time for such a command; EffectLifecycleScheduler.cs:770-787 leaves an until_time lifetime unchanged when CurrentTime is absent.
Rules/Block_23.A.txt:19-40 and Rules/Block_2.txt:668-679 explicitly define calendar-only setWorldTime, including plot time skips and time travel.
confirmed_material_findings.defect: R2 stores time as prefix/remainder {from,to} intervals, says to normalize canonical [from,to] before publication, and routes an uncomputable interval to ordinary validation/repair semantics. The actual ordinary contract has an accepted unresolved/fail-open result, not that repair requirement. The declared closed shape does not define an accepted unresolved projection. Generic promises to preserve resolver semantics in T195 do not resolve the contradictory concrete interval contract.
confirmed_material_findings.consequence: A faithful implementation of the stated interval/repair branch would reject or stall a lawful result, or invent a numeric/zero interval to complete it. Both violate the full ordinary-outcome requirement and can alter effect/progression behavior.
confirmed_material_findings.requested_change: Make the time projection explicitly distinguish resolved incremental/absolute time from an accepted unresolved absolute command. Retain raw source bytes and each genuine owner's actual result, including progression fallback/report handling and nullable effect CurrentTime. Require numeric intervals only when the actual source resolves them; do not infer elapsed duration from an absolute jump or add a calendar-conversion policy implicitly. Add a future acceptance case for calendar-only setWorldTime, plus resolved absolute/rewind and genuine elapsed cases. Any stronger conversion policy is a separate proposed dependency/grant.
confirmed_material_findings.validation_status: STATIC_SOURCE_CONFIRMED; runtime reproduction and tests UNRUN by task restriction

hypotheses_and_optional_improvements.title: Make the immutable action-boundary seal relationship explicit
hypotheses_and_optional_improvements.assessment: The old closed basis field list does not name action inputs, while actionBoundary is a sibling containing mutable acknowledgements. R2 nevertheless requires source capture to bind the action capability, and the plan requires S/B/C binding before CommonAuthority/input/prepared sealing. I did not confirm a bypass or an impossible DAG: those provisions can cover the immutable action inputs through S and the common proof. Before accepting D9 schemas, explicitly state which immutable boundary/roster/time inputs enter S/raw basis/common proof, which fields are mutable overlays, and how cold reconstruction validates each. This is a precision risk, not a confirmed material defect in the current dependency proposal.

hypotheses_and_optional_improvements.title: Specify original absence evidence for reply-dependent generated paths
hypotheses_and_optional_improvements.assessment: A new item/content/location-related path named only by the reply cannot gain absent-before authority from a missing dictionary entry or from its current submitted bytes. PendingTurnSnapshotReader distinguishes selected bytes, authenticated absence, and mere declared paths. R2 already requires exact owner catalogs/absence maps and makes their reconciliation a pre-grant T193-T195 dependency; it does not explicitly authorize that shortcut. Add this concrete boundary and a future new-path negative case to the dependency deliverable. No current runtime defect or unconditional coverage failure was established.

assessment: The design now distinguishes request identity from game action/turn n, preserves source-prefix effects, requires real Plan/ValidatedEmpty ordinary completion and rejects treating missing family support as successful HOLD.

FD reservation, atomic FT, child-original-to-FD-to-parent proof, retained artifacts, candidate-only repair, shared M acknowledgement and same-turn separate story witness are addressed as proposed work; no current implementation proof is claimed.

The 182-name table is accurate as a DTO/mapping coverage inventory. It correctly does not treat mapped names or paths as Mortal write authority; canonical-only and dynamic companions remain owner-catalog reconciliation work.

The universal pure composite is substantially wider than the former three-family F1. T192-T198 and D9-D11 expose that scope instead of claiming existing StateDistributor/normalizer or lifecycle handlers are sufficient.

T197 honestly requires a separately designed durable MortalDeath-to-LifeEvaluation target receipt and exact cohorts before activation; existing handler source is sequential and is not represented as an existing durable acknowledgement. The actual destination LifeEvaluation turn remains genuine.
D4 allocator, guided US5, D8 narrow raw-payload/earned-XP limits, actual DOM/visual and Linux/Windows qualification remain open. No demonstrated F1 obstacle selects F2.
